title: [FancyZones] "Custom layout not found" error after closing editor
author: SeraphimaZykova
summary: In an RDP session, closing the FancyZones editor can leave the selected custom layout unapplied and log 'Custom layout not found' even though the layout exists in custom-layouts.json.
next_action: Reproduce current RDP editor close/apply flow and trace the selected custom layout identifier across process boundaries.

confidence.rationale: The transition and error are concrete, but current identity handling must be traced.

judgment.rationale: The report provides deterministic RDP steps, a control layout, the exact error text, and a diagnostic archive.
evidence: The failure occurs after selecting a non-Priority custom layout in an RDP session and closing the editor.
Shift-drag shows that the chosen layout is not active.
The log says Custom layout not found while the layout remains in custom-layouts.json.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce current RDP editor close/apply flow and trace the selected custom layout identifier across process boundaries.

fix_assessment.rationale: The report localizes the transition but does not prove whether monitor identity, editor parameters, or data reload loses the layout.

issue_context.summary: In an RDP session, closing the FancyZones editor can leave the selected custom layout unapplied and log 'Custom layout not found' even though the layout exists in custom-layouts.json.
known_information: The issue requires an RDP connection and multiple monitors in the described setup.
Priority Zone behaves differently from the custom layout.
inferences: RDP display identity changes may cause the editor's selected layout reference to mismatch runtime data after editor exit.
issue_context.analysis: The exact error and archive support a maintainer-side trace without another reporter request.
initial_investigation: Read the extracted report and diagnostic link.
Confirmed current FancyZones includes EditorParameters and FancyZonesData/AppZoneHistory paths relevant to editor-to-runtime state.

actions.label: Reproduce RDP custom-layout loss
actions.note: Maintainer-side verification only; this artifact performs no upstream write.

reproduce.title: Trace custom layout selection after closing the editor over RDP
prerequisites: Remote Windows test machine with current PowerToys
At least one saved custom layout
setup: Connect through RDP and launch the FancyZones editor.
Select a custom layout other than Priority Grid.
steps: Shift-drag a window and verify the selected layout is active.
Inspect logs for Custom layout not found.
Compare the selected layout identifier with custom-layouts.json and the active monitor/desktop identifier.
reproduce.expected_result: The selected custom layout should remain active after the editor closes, with no missing-layout error.
